article_title: The Effect of Herrmann Whole Brain Teaching Method on Students' Understanding of Simple Electric Circuits
citation: Ali Khalid Ali Bawaneh, Ahmad Nurulazam Md Zain, & Salmiza Saleh. (2010). The Effect of Herrmann Whole Brain Teaching Method on Students' Understanding of Simple Electric Circuits. European Journal of Physics Education, Vol. 2 No. 2, ISSN 1309 7202. https://portal.issn.org/resource/ISSN/13097202
title: HWBTM lesson structure: all four learning styles fulfilled within a single lesson
description: The Herrmann Whole Brain Teaching Method organizes each lesson so that every one of the four learning styles (A, B, C, D) is served: the article states that "each of the four lea rning styles (A, B, C, and D) were fulfilled in a single lesson," with a student's preferred style used in one quarter of classroom time. Lessons begin with brainstorming questions linking new to prior knowledge, then student experiments and activities, teacher demonstrations without giving answers, group discussions, application worksheets, and homework. The pattern makes the student the hub of the learning-teaching process.
requirements: Teachers receive training on the method (the article reports two one-hour training sessions for experimental teachers)
Instructional content prepared to suit the various learning styles demonstrated by classroom students
constraints: Evaluated only for two weeks across four class periods on one electric-circuits topic in eighth grade
examples: Students collected data, installed devices, graphed interrelations between variables, and reported while doing experiments; teachers performed demonstrations preceded by questioning without giving the correct answers
